forest.statement:
Optimize on one NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3. Use the actual AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy.
Compute one FP32 sum(abs(x)) for n FP32 values. Performance n=268435456 (exactly 1 GiB of input). Checks include 1,127,1024,1048576 and performance n. input1=x; other inputs ignored; output one float; scratch n+65536 floats. Each call must reset/overwrite output. Compare to an independent FP64 sum with absolute error <=.001+2e-4*abs(reference). Allocation and transfers excluded; all launches and necessary resets included.
Edit only src/candidate.cu. Preserve extern C void run(const void*x,const void*k,const void*gy,void*out,void*scratch,int n,int h,int l,int ks). All pointers are device memory owned by the host. Use the default CUDA stream. Do not read beyond buffers. Scratch is not guaranteed initialized. No external optimized library calls; ordinary CUDA primitives and CUB block primitives are allowed.
No cached answers, filesystem or environment inspection, timing inspection, phase detection, or external tools. Every call must compute on the current input. Immutable reference implementations and correctness checks are withheld from source. Choose useful topics independently, record failures, complete memory integration and independently confirm final G. No additional allocations or devices.

decision.rationale: Partir du meilleur essai mesuré et correct (a0f, 0,288230 ms) et tester son mapping float2 à 128 threads avec la politique de partiels T1 plafonnée à 4096. Les hybrides précédents à 4096 et 8192 partiels étaient plus lents; cette combinaison est une hypothèse distincte, pas un gain présumé. Mesurer l’appel complet et valider tous les cas.

Le premier hybride plafonné à 4096 partiels a mesuré 0,304724 ms, contre 0,288230 ms pour a0f; l’hybride antérieur à 4096 a aussi été plus lent. Tester la politique adaptative ceil(n/4096) avec plafond 1024: elle conserve le nombre de partiels de a0f au grand n tout en réduisant les CTAs aux tailles plus petites. Maintenir le mapping float2 et corriger l’owner de la dernière valeur impaire par modulo du nombre de partiels. Gain non présumé; vérifier correction et temps complet.
The last hybrid was correct but substantially slower than its base (0.450423988 s vs 0.288230395 s). Read its exact source to identify a concrete contrast for the next integration.

Test whether the slow dynamic hybrid’s runtime partial-count loop and stride costs can be avoided at the maximum grid size without abandoning its adaptive count for smaller inputs. Keep a0f’s paired float2/scalar mapping; use the 4096-element target and modulo tail ownership from the hybrid, but add a compile-time-specialized max-count path for both kernels. The earlier hybrids were correct but measured 0.304724 ms and 0.450424 ms versus a0f at 0.288230 ms; this tests a hypothesis, not a presumed speedup.

After three correct integrations, none beats the measured a0f reference (0.288230 ms): the latest compile-time-specialized hybrid measured 0.288373 ms, while the earlier hybrids measured 0.304724 ms and 0.450424 ms. The latest difference is very small and does not establish a repeatable gain. Further changes lack a supported hypothesis; leave final selection and independent confirmation to the controller.

children.objective: Build a two-stage fused sum(abs(x)) with simple contiguous scalar loads and a conventional per-CTA reduction. Explore global work partitioning: vary first-stage partial count/granularity and the finalizer’s fan-in so the large input is sufficiently parallel while finalization stays cheap. Leave vectorized loads and thread/block mapping to T3. Every consumed partial must be written in the current call, and the finalizer must overwrite output. Validate all required sizes and the stated FP64 error bound; compare full-call time.
children.subject: Hierarchical fusion: partial granularity and finalization

children.objective: Evaluate a distinct single-kernel alternative: reset output in the default stream, stream input once, reduce locally per CTA, then atomicAdd one CTA result to output. Explore keeping CTA atomic count modest; do not rely on scratch initialization or omit the per-call reset. Compare total time including reset and launch overhead against hierarchical candidates, and validate every required size and the FP64 tolerance.
children.subject: Single-kernel CTA aggregation with output atomics

children.objective: Use the two-stage fused topology as a controlled starting point. Hold global input tile boundaries, partial count, and finalizer organization fixed for each comparison; explore within-CTA streaming and reduction mapping, including multiple accumulators, suitable contiguous/vector loads, and CTA dimensions or work per thread. Handle alignment and tails for every valid input. Do not retune global partitioning or finalizer fan-in, which T1 owns. Validate all required sizes and the stated FP64 error bound, and measure full-call time.

The baseline’s 1.228 ms mean is the only supplied measurement; any ranking must use correct candidates and comparable full-call timings.
